title: Admin control security review — RBAC v2, SSO/SAML hardening, and audit logging remediation
creator: Sophie Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a consolidated remediation plan to address findings from the March 2026 penetration test and our internal threat modeling exercise across four related areas: RBAC v2 (role model and enforcement surfaces), admin controls & privileged session management, SSO/SAML configuration and assertion verification, and audit logging (retention, tamper-resistance, and SIEM integration).

Background:
- Recent pentest (report id: PT-2026-03) surfaced several privilege escalation and assertion-handling issues affecting admin endpoints and RBAC enforcement paths.
- Parallel threat model (doc: Confluence/PlatformSecurity/RBAC-SSO-ThreatModel) highlighted attacker TTPs that exploit inconsistent authorization checks across API gateway, console, and private deployment admin plane.
- ENG-7321 contains prior RBAC v2 scope work; this ticket focuses on risk remediation, cross-team verification, and operational controls (audit + SSO hardening) required for production rollout.

Scope (in-scope):
- Code and config changes to close enumerated pentest findings for admin APIs and console admin functions.
- Strengthening SAML assertion validation (audience, recipient, assertion encryption, clock skew, authnContext mapping).
- RBAC v2 enforcement audit: canonicalize enforcement points and add end-to-end tests.
- Audit logging improvements: immutable append-only logs, enrichment with actor/context, longer retention for admin events, and safe export to SIEM.
- Run follow-up red-team validation and update e2e test harness.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full RBAC redesign (handled by ENG-7321 planning) beyond targeted fixes.
- Cross-region SIEM ingestion capacity changes (separate infra ticket if needed).

Pen-test & Threat Model Findings (high level):
1) Privilege escalation via inconsistent role checks: some admin endpoints checked role names but not permission bits; others depended on client-side UI gating only. (Severity: High)
2) SAML: missing audience and recipient checks in our SAML consumer led to assert replay possibilities when combined with lax session invalidation. (Severity: High)
3) Audit logs: admin actions logged but lacked stable request identifiers, and logs were writable by an admin process prior to ingestion (integrity risk). (Severity: Medium)
4) Privileged session management: long-lived admin sessions without step-up authentication for sensitive operations. (Severity: Medium)
5) Tooling & observability gaps: lack of end-to-end tests that include SAML assertion tampering and RBAC negative-paths. (Severity: Medium)

Remediation Plan (by area):
A) RBAC v2 enforcement hardening:
- Action: Canonicalize the authorization middleware to a single enforcement library used by API gateway, console backend, and private agent. Replace scattered role-name checks with permission-bit checks and policy evaluation.
- Deliverables: enforcement library PR, migration guide, deprecation warnings, and automated test matrix mapping roles->permissions.
- Risk/Trade-off: One migration point may cause short-lived 500s if not backward compatible. Use feature-flagged rollout and a canary guard.

B) SSO/SAML hardening:
- Action: Enforce strict SAML validation (audience, recipient, InResponseTo, AuthnInstant clock skew <= 60s), require signed assertions, validate signature algorithms, and introduce assertion replay cache keyed by assertion ID per identity provider.
- Deliverables: saml-consumer library update, config schema changes for identity providers, integration tests with malicious assertion samples.
- Risk/Trade-off: Some IdPs in customer environments send non-standard attributes; add opt-in compatibility flags and plan manual onboarding for legacy IdPs.

C) Admin controls & privileged session management:
- Action: Add step-up MFA for critical admin actions (user deletion, role assignment, key rotation). Reduce default admin session TTL from 12h to 1h with refresh token rotation and inactivity timeout. Log step-up events.
- Deliverables: console UX change spec (PM/Design), backend step-up endpoint, updated session management library.
- Risk/Trade-off: UX impact for on-call can be mitigated by allowlisting emergency sessions with stricter audit.

D) Audit logging & log integrity:
- Action: Add immutable log write pipeline (append-only S3 + signed manifests) and include stable request_id, actor_id, effective_permissions, and originating_ip in each admin event. Configure retention 1y for admin events and ship to Splunk/Datadog in near-real time.
- Deliverables: logging schema, ingestion pipeline PRs, retention policy config, SIEM dashboards for admin anomalies.
- Risk/Trade-off: Storage and ingestion costs; limit to admin-class events and sample verbose payloads.

Implementation plan & rollout:
- Week 1 (this ticket): implement critical RBAC fixes for endpoints flagged by pentest (API gateway + console), SAML audience/recipient checks, and assertion replay cache. Add unit tests and integration test harness.
- Week 2: deploy to staging, run automated negative-path tests and the pentest regression suite, author migration guide, and open a phased canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Week 3: enable step-up MFA for a subset of orgs, activate extended audit retention, and run red-team verification.
- Post-rollout: schedule an external pen-test follow-up and update SOC runbooks.

Verification & Acceptance Criteria:
- All pentest high findings closed or mitigated with compensating controls and documented in PT-2026-03 follow-up section.
- Integration tests for assertion tampering and RBAC negative paths pass in staging and canary.
- Audit events for admin flows contain required fields and are routed to SIEM.
- Step-up MFA flow enforced on critical admin actions in canary orgs.
- No customer-facing outages during canary rollout (rollback plan exists).

Artifacts & Links:
- Pen-test report (PT-2026-03): drive.redwood/sec/pt-2026-03.pdf
- Threat model: drive.redwood/sec/rbac-sso-threat-model-2026.md
- Related ticket: sources/linear/engineering/ENG-7321-rbacv2-attack-surface-remediation.json
- Design/console step-up mockups: drive.redwood/design/console-stepup-v2.png
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls (PRs will be linked here as created)

Open questions / blockers:
1) IdP compatibility: which enterprise customers need compatibility flags? PM to gather list and approve tolerations.
2) SIEM ingestion capacity/cost: infra needs to confirm budget for 1y retention of admin events.
3) Legal/compliance retention policy: small nations/regulatory rules may require different retention — coordinate with Legal.
